subject: Clarify billing split: streaming vs session minima and packaging options
messages:
From: Claire Ng <claire@ledgerai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@ledgerai.com>, Adam Feldman <adam.feldman@ledgerai.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question: minima and streaming sessions

Hi Tessa,

Quick question as we finalize the SOW: LedgerAI will be instrumenting a mix of short API calls (per-request inference) and long-lived streaming connections for conversational workflows. Our procurement/legal team is asking how Redwood applies the "minimum charge" (per-session or per-billing-line) across these two modes. Specifically:

- If we have a long-lived streaming session that emits tokens over multiple days, does it consume the same minimum bucket as many short calls, or is it billed differently?
- How do committed-pack discounts interact with the minima? If we buy a 100k token monthly commitment plus an additional streaming pack, will minima on individual sessions still apply?

Can you point to an example invoice or scenario we can show our finance folks? We also want to understand rounding behavior (do you round up per-call, per-minute, per-token quantum?).

Thanks — appreciate a concise example we can include in the procurement packet.

— Claire
Senior PM, LedgerAI

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@ledgerai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question: minima and streaming sessions

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer first, then an example invoice scenario attached.

Summary answers:
- Streaming sessions are metered by tokens emitted (streamed) and by the session type. The minimum charge applies at the invoice line level, which is tied to the SKU you use ("per-call" SKU vs "streaming" SKU). That means a long-lived streaming session is charged against the streaming SKU minima, not the short-call minima, so it won't amortize into per-call minima buckets.
- Committed token packs are applied first to token consumption across SKUs; minima still exist on each SKU line but we can apply an initial credit to cover minima for the first billing period when negotiating.
- Rounding: we operate on token quanta of 100 tokens for metering; rounding up occurs at the invoice line level after aggregation for the billing window. We do not round per single API call unless the call is the only activity for that invoice line.

Attached: redwood-pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx — includes an example invoice for a hybrid month. Below is a pared-down scenario for your finance team.

Example scenario (October billing window):
- Committed pack: 100,000 tokens (applies across SKUs)
- Actual consumption: 60k tokens from short calls (per-call SKU), 55k tokens streamed from long sessions (streaming SKU)
- Billing behavior:
  * Apply 100k committed pack: 100k covers 115k consumed total -> remaining committed = 0
  * Invoice lines still evaluate minima by SKU: streaming SKU has a 10k monthly minimum; per-call SKU has a 1k minimum. Because both SKUs have positive consumption, minima don't trigger additional charge in this month.
  * Rounding: token tallies are aggregated per-SKU then rounded to 100-token quanta.

If you want, Marissa and I can propose two concession paths for contract language: (A) waive first-month minima on streaming SKU as a one-time onboarding credit, or (B) offer a blended SKU for high-volume customers that lumps streaming and per-call into a single billing line (this requires a 6–12 month commit).

Looping in Marissa for commercial terms and Karthik for confirmation on how the invoices are produced.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Billing question: minima and streaming sessions

Tessa / Karthik — quick internal notes before we lock the SOW. A few follow-ups from procurement we should anticipate:

1) Proration ask: LedgerAI wants the minima to be prorated if they ramp mid-month (they're onboarding incremental traffic). We normally prorate committed packs but not minima — is there a way to present a pragmatic exception?
2) Invoice sample: procurement will want a line-by-line sample showing the math when committed pack is exhausted and when minima bites. Let's create two small tables: (A) under-commit month (minima would have triggered), (B) over-commit month (no minima).
3) Packaging ask: If we suggest blended SKU (per Tessa), what discount do we need to offer to make it attractive vs keeping separate SKUs? I suggest we offer 10% off list for blended annual commit and waive streaming minima for first two invoices.

Karthik — what's the operational impact of offering a blended SKU (billing pipeline + runtime labeling)? Can we produce a single invoice line that consumes committed pack first and enforces a single minima? If not, we need to be explicit.

— Marissa
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Billing question: minima and streaming sessions

Marissa / Tessa — technical constraints and feasible options: 

- Current billing system binds minima to invoice lines which are created per SKU. We can create a blended invoice line, but it requires creating a "composite SKU" during provisioning and tagging traffic accordingly. It's not impossible but takes ~2–3 business days of SKU provisioning + QA.
- Proration: we can prorate minima for the first partial month as a policy exception; implementing automated prorated minima would need a small batching change and a short release (2 weeks). For fast deals, we can handle the first 2 months as manual credits (no code changes).
- Rounding / quantum: implementation aggregates token counts per SKU per billing window, then applies ceil(token_count / 100) * 100 for chargeable units. That means edge cases where a single stream emits 120 tokens across multiple small heartbeats will get aggregated before rounding, minimizing waste.

Recommended path for LedgerAI:
1) Create a composite SKU for the customer during onboarding so LedgerAI sees one invoice line and one minima. Provide 10% blended discount for a 12-month commit. Provision composite SKU in 2–3 business days.
2) Operational concession: waive streaming minima for first two invoices (manual credits if needed).
3) Deliver a sample invoice PDF showing both an under-commit and over-commit month.

If Sales signs off, we can schedule SKU provisioning immediately and include the exact concession language in the SOW.

— Karthik
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@ledgerai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@ledgerai.com>
Date: Thu, 31 Oct 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question: minima and streaming sessions — proposed commercial offer

Hi Claire — thanks for the patience. Based on our internal discussion, here's a concise offer we can include in the SOW: 

Offer summary (final):
- Composite billing line: we'll provision a blended SKU for LedgerAI so both streaming and per-call consumption are invoiced on a single line (single minima applies).
- Discount: 10% off list pricing for a 12-month commitment (Deal: LDG-2029-0443).
- Minima concession: waive the composite SKU minima for the first two invoices; thereafter the composite SKU minima applies monthly.
- Proration: first partial month will be prorated manually in the invoice if ramping occurs mid-month (we'll provide an immediate credit if needed).
- Rounding: tokens aggregated per billing window and rounded to 100-token quanta at invoice line level.

Next steps we propose:
1) I'll attach the SOW and pricing matrix (attached). If that looks good, we'll provision the composite SKU (2–3 business days) and send a DocuSign for the SOW.
2) You asked for a sample invoice scenario — we will send two PDFs: under-commit and over-commit examples.
3) If procurement signs off on the above, we'll issue the DocuSign link (see related link) with the concession language inserted.

Let me know if you'd like the waiver to be one invoice instead of two; we can do that if Finance prefers.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx, SOW-draft.pdf
